newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria urges Liberian victor to unify country.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria urges Liberian victor to unify country.

text.p: Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha, the architect of a peace plan that ended seven years of civil war in Liberia, on Friday urged the winner of the country's presidential election to unify the nation.

"I hope you will seize this opportunity which has been provided by the elections, to unify the country, once again and create an atmosphere of trust and confidence which cuts across every stratum of the Liberian society," Abacha said in a congratulatory message to president-elect Charles Taylor.
"Your victory is a clear testimony of the trust and confidence which the people of Liberia repose in you," he said.

Taylor, the former warlord who set off the Liberian civil war in 1989 when he invaded from Ivory Coast, won a landslide in the poll staged on Saturday to consolidate the peace brokered for his country by the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) of which Abacha is chairman.

A Nigeria-dominated ECOMOG force, which intervened in Liberia in 1990 to stop the carnage, successfully disarmed the armed factions this year, paving the way for peace after a war which has killed more than 150,000 people and displaced half the pre-war population of 2.5 million.
A letter from the Liberian independent electoral commission to Nigerian rulers released to the press hailed the country for its contributions to the Liberian peace process.
"Nigeria's role in shaping a new Africa will one day, no matter how grudgingly, be the subject of worldwide acclaim," said the letter signed by commission chairman Henry Andrews.
Nigeria is currently shunned by Western nations for lack of democracy and alleged human rights abuses.
Abacha has promised to hand over to an elected president next year but critics say his democracy plan is skewed to perpetuate his hold on power.
